newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Commerce Commission warns gas industry.
newsitem.headline: NZ Commerce Commission warns gas industry.

text.p: The New Zealand Commerce Commission warned the gas industry on Tuesday that if the 1980 wholesale contracts were not successfully renegotiated within a reasonable time, then the commission would consider court action against gas companies.
The commission's Chief Investigating officer of the Network Industries Unit, David Taylor, said the commission's view was that 1980 contracts were anti-competitive and a breach of the Commerce Act.
The commission's concerns about the contracts were:
* the requirement that the utility buy all its gas from the Natural Gas Corp
* the restriction on NGC competing with utilities
* the requirement that new delivery points be mutually agreed, effectively preventing a utility entering another's area
The gas industry was deregulated in 1993 when the government removed price controls.
Taylor said the commission was increasingly frustrated that new contracts had not been put in place.
"Therefore, it is appropriate to remind the parties of one incentive that they share in common -- namely that they are all potentially subject to remedies under the Act."
He said if the commission was satisfied a breach of the Act had occurred then it could take enforcement action in the High Court. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
